extracted.intended_audience: general readers, music fans, festival-goers, and researchers seeking information about the Bonnaroo festival
extracted.subtask_description: A descriptive encyclopedic profile of a single American multi-day music festival (Bonnaroo), covering history, organization, lineup characteristics, venue, attendance, sustainability, and notable moments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre diversity of lineup
rubrics_metrics.description: "Its multiple stages feature stylistically diverse music, including indie rock, classic rock, world music, hip hop, jazz, Americana, bluegrass, country music, folk, gospel, reggae, pop, electronic, and other alternative music."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The festival programs a very wide range of musical styles across stages; diversity of genres is a core characteristic and selling point. Examples and full genre list are provided in the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: "Second Thursday in June, duration of four days"; "Musical acts begin on Wednesday evening and end on Sunday night."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bonnaroo is structured as a multi-day (four-day) festival with pre-opening performances; timing (second Thursday in June) and daily scheduling (Wed–Sun music) are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location and venue scale
rubrics_metrics.description: "Bonnaroo has taken place at what is now Great Stage Park, a 700-acre (280 ha) farm in Manchester, Tennessee."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Site size and rural/farm setting (Great Stage Park) are central to the festival's identity and logistics; venue scale affects camping, stages, and crowd management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage infrastructure and adaptability
rubrics_metrics.description: "Centeroo stages include the What Stage, Which Stage, That Tent, This Tent, and The Other Stage (previously 'The Other Tent', but changed to a full stage to accommodate the growth of EDM at the festival)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage lineup and the ability to convert/upgrade infrastructure (e.g., tent to full stage) to reflect changing genres (EDM growth) is an evaluative dimension of production and programming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary activities and programming
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond music, Bonnaroo offered comedy and cinema in a dedicated tent (removed in 2008) and "various artistic, environmental, and community activities... parades, dance shows, yoga, sustainability lessons, a 5k run, a marriage barn, a water slide, vendor markets, and more."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The festival's non-musical offerings (arts, wellness, community activities) contribute to attendee experience and distinguish the event; program changes over time (e.g., removal of comedy/cinema tent) are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmentalism and sustainability practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Bonnaroo "actively supports recycling and sustainability." It was recognized by A Greener Festival for multiple years; "In 2004 Bonnaroo said it prevented having to collect 120 tons of trash by encouraging fans to recycle. Food and drink are sold in organic and recyclable materials to create less waste. AGF auditors review festivals, as well as requiring their self-evaluation. As of late, Bonnaroo has initiated many 'green' activities during the festival, such as Planet Roo."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Environmental initiatives, third‑party recognition (A Greener Festival), material choices for vendors, and internal auditing/self-evaluation are presented as concrete sustainability practices and metrics to assess the festival's green performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic impact and charitable work
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2009 the Bonnaroo Works Fund was created as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit awarding grants to local non-profits and schools. By 2013 the direct and indirect economic impact since inception was estimated at $51 million (including $2.9 million in tax revenue for 2012). In 2023, Bonnaroo contributed $339.8 million to the regional economy (including over $5.1 million in tax revenue) and created or supported 4,163 full-time job equivalents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The festival's local economic contribution, tax revenue, job creation, and charitable activities (grant-making via Bonnaroo Works Fund) are quantifiable dimensions used to evaluate its regional impact and social value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical reception and accolades
rubrics_metrics.description: The festival was ranked in 2003 by Rolling Stone as one of the "50 Moments That Changed Rock & Roll", called "Festival of the Decade" by Consequence of Sound, and listed among the 10 Best Festivals by GQ. Rolling Stone in 2008 called it "the ultimate over-the-top summer festival"; The New York Times said "Bonnaroo has revolutionized the modern rock festival" in 2012; Billboard named it the 8th best music festival in 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press coverage, rankings, and industry accolades are catalogued as indicators of reputation and cultural significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance and popularity metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Attendance figures are listed (e.g., "70,000 (2024)"), with an annual attendance table for years 2002–2025 showing fluctuations (peaks, declines, cancellations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yearly attendance numbers and trends (including growth, decline, and recovery) serve as quantitative measures of popularity and capacity. The article includes detailed year-by-year figures and notes on estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event risk management and cancellations
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2020 event was pushed back and ultimately canceled because of COVID-19. The 2021 event was canceled due to torrential rainfall from Hurricane Ida making grounds unsuitable for vehicle traffic. In 2025, the day after its Thursday night opening, the festival was cancelled due to severe weather.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellations for public‑health or weather reasons are highlighted; contingency planning, weather risk mitigation, and resilience are implicit evaluative considerations for event organizers and attendees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media and streaming partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: "Hulu has exclusively streamed the festival from 2022 to 2024, alongside Austin City Limits Music Festival and Lollapalooza."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusive streaming deals and media partnerships extend audience reach and are a metric of commercial/media strategy and visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founding, organization, and ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Bonnaroo was developed and founded by Superfly Presents and AC Entertainment; launched in 2002 by Ashley Capps, Superfly, Coran Capshaw and Chip Hooper. In 2019 Live Nation bought out Superfly's share of Bonnaroo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Founders, producing organizations, and ownership changes are relevant to understanding governance, strategic direction, and potential commercial shifts in programming or operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable performances and curated events
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of high-profile or unique performances include D'Angelo's surprise 2012 Superjam return to American stages and the Beastie Boys' final show at the festival in 2009. The festival has hosted curated events such as the Superjam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Singular performances, surprise appearances, and curated collaborative events build festival prestige and historical significance; such moments are documented as highlights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camping, community culture, and comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Bonnaroo has been referred to as "the Glastonbury Festival of the United States" based on similarities: camping, a sense of community, and a large farmground location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Camping culture, community ethos, and experiential comparisons to other major festivals are used to characterize attendee experience and festival identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Campground-stage relationships and late-night programming
rubrics_metrics.description: Outeroo stages in the campgrounds vary year-to-year, but have included a Where in the Woods Stage since 2018, which exclusively offers electronic music shows during late night hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placement of stages in campground areas and programming for late-night audiences (e.g., electronic music in Outeroo) indicate deliberate segmentation of experiences and scheduling for different attendee needs.
